chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Ayub, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) said:

All goodness has been gathered in three traits: reflection, silence, and speech. Every reflection in which there is no consideration is an omission, and every silence in which there is no thought is inattention, and every speech in which there is no remembrance (of Allah) is nonsense. Hence, Tuba (bliss) is for the one whose reflection is a lesson, whose silence is a thought, and whose speech is remembrance (of Allah), and who weeps over his mistake, and from whom people are safe from his evil.
ai.seo_question: What are the three essential traits for gathering all goodness according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: Attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and tracing back to Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), this hadith from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* presents a triad of spiritual disciplines where *nazar* (observation) becomes *'ibrah* (lesson), *sukut* (silence) becomes *fikrah* (contemplation), and *kalam* (speech) becomes *dhikr* (remembrance). This framework emphasizes that mere physical acts are insufficient; they must be infused with conscious awareness to prevent spiritual negligence (*sahw*) and idle talk (*laghw*). The culmination in weeping for one's sins highlights the link between self-reflection and social security (*aman al-nas sharahu*), a key concept in Shia ethical theology.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Muhammed bin Isa bin ‘Ubaid, from Yunus bin Abdul-Rahman, from Abu Ayub, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, that he said: The Commander of the Believers, peace be upon him, said:

All goodness has been gathered in three traits: reflection, silence and speech. Every reflection in which there is no consideration, is an omission. Every silence in which there is no thought, is inattention. Every speech in which there is no mentioning (of Allah), is nonsense. Hence, Tuba is for the one whose reflection is a lesson, whose silence is a thought and whose speech is mentioning (of Allah), and who weeps due to his mistake and whom people are at safety from (any potential of) his evil.
